title: RoutingTable
description: Normative shape of the routing table for agent/contracts/role-routing@0.1.0 - one table per account, created when the first profile is saved, edited only through settings, and validated against this file before it is saved. The six roles are enumerated from the product and are all required to be present, because a role that is absent from the table is how one quietly acquires an implicit default (INV-AG-24). The table carries no member beyond the two it declares: a table-wide fallback profile is the substitution rule arriving by the back door, which INV-AG-23 forbids. The split the defaults propose is the measured one - VERIFIED (spikes/SP-17-provider-matrix/REPORT.md#1-tra-loi-tung-cau-hoi Q1, Q3, Q6).

tableVersion.description: The version of the role-routing contract this table was written against. The table replicates between devices on different builds: a newer build reads an older table unchanged, and an older build meeting a newer version refuses the whole table (TABLE_VERSION_AHEAD), because reading around an unrecognised member here would mean running a role on a model the user assigned to something else.

assignments.description: Exactly six members, always present. An unassigned role is represented by the explicit unassigned state and never by the key being absent.

Assignment.description: What a role points at, or the explicit statement that it points at nothing. An assignment carries no capability list of its own: those facts belong to agent/contracts/provider-profile@0.1.0, and a second copy here would be the one that goes stale when the user edits the profile - stale in the direction that sends an image to a model that can no longer read one.

acknowledgedUnmeasured.description: True when the user confirmed an assignment the product holds no measurement for. The product does not enforce a judgement it has no way to make; it states what was measured and records that the user decided anyway.
